title: How local is a free-float laboratory?
promptMarkdown: Two initially comoving test particles in a falling laboratory have separation $L=2\,\mathrm m$. Their measured relative acceleration is approximately $\ddot L=\kappa L$, with $\kappa=3.0\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ over the short experiment. The apparatus detects a change in separation of $10\,\mu\mathrm m$. Estimate the longest observation time for which a constant-separation inertial model stays within that tolerance. Check the short-time approximation, explain how halving $L$ changes the bound, and explain why one particle alone would not supply this tidal test.
hintLadder: Integrate the relative acceleration twice over a short interval.
Check $\kappa t^2$ rather than simply calling the time short.
Keep the absolute detection threshold fixed when changing $L$.
